title: The refractive index of the medium within the volume of deep inelastic $ep$ scattering: I. Group velocity of interaction carriers
abstract: We propose a new method for measuring several characteristics of a fermion-boson medium formed during deep inelastic particle scattering. This method involves measuring the group and phase velocities of the accompanying wave process. The phase and group velocities of a wave process are related by the Rayleigh differential condition. The refractive index of a medium is determined by the phase velocity, while the group velocity characterises the medium's dispersion properties. In the case of deep inelastic $ep$ scattering under consideration, the wave process in an individual event is understood to be the exchange between an electron and a proton of an effective, non-perturbative mediator of interaction (${\cal B}$) with the quantum numbers of a neutral current. In the first report, we present new data on the group velocity of interaction carriers ${\cal B}$. We extracted the group velocity modulus values, $U_{_{\cal B}}^*$, from the HERA collider data using a formula derived from modified Heisenberg uncertainty relations and applying the indirect measurement method.. etc...(see preprint text)
summary: This paper investigates the speed of the virtual mediator boson in deep inelastic scattering by treating the interaction region as a dispersive medium. It develops a theoretical framework relating group and phase velocities and applies it to HERA data. The key finding is that the derived speed can exceed the speed of light and exhibits strong singularities as the virtual boson's energy approaches zero.
main_problem: The paper proposes a novel method to measure the characteristics of a fermion-boson medium formed during deep inelastic electron-proton scattering by analyzing the group and phase velocities of the mediating wave process.
main_result: Analysis of HERA data suggests that the effective mediator boson's speed can exceed the speed of light in free space, and the derived model shows a strong, singular dependence on the virtual boson's energy ($q_0$) as $q_0$ approaches zero.
method: The authors use the Rayleigh differential condition and derive expressions for group and phase velocities from a relativistic dispersion relation model, comparing these theoretical predictions against indirect measurements from HERA collider data.
model_or_system: The physical system is deep inelastic $ep$ scattering, where the interaction is mediated by an effective, non-perturbative boson ($B$). The analysis utilizes a relativistic dispersion relation model ($\omega^2 = \omega_0^2 + c^2 \sum k_i^2$) to define the velocities.
key_observables: Group velocity modulus ($U^*_B$), Phase velocity ($V^*_B$), Normalized speed ($ eta^*$), and the absorption mean free path ($L^*$).
important_parameters: Kinematic variables like $Q^2$, Bjorken variable $x$, and the virtual boson energy $q_0$. The analysis focuses on the limits $q_0 	o 0$ and $y 	o 1$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the applicability of the Rayleigh condition and relies on deriving velocity estimates from modified Heisenberg uncertainty relations and specific kinematic limits.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the kinematic view of the scattering process, the dependence of the normalized speed ($ eta^*$) on $q_0$ (showing divergence near $q_0=0$), and the extracted $ eta^*$ vs. $Q^2$ from HERA II data.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the theoretical framework (velocity definitions, Rayleigh condition), applying this framework to the DIS process, deriving model predictions for $ eta^*(q_0)$, and finally comparing these model results against actual HERA experimental data across various kinematic limits.
why_interesting: While the core physics is high-energy particle physics, the methodology—using dispersion relations and velocity measurements to probe medium properties—shares conceptual overlap with how collective excitations are studied in condensed matter systems.
